challenges.name: narrow-tools-quiz
challenges.title: Whose data can the tool read, and what stops a duplicate plan?
challenges.description: Two statements about the redesigned Study-Plan tools: whether a session-bound get_progress can still be pointed at another learner, and whether a tool annotation prevents a retried create_study_plan from saving two plans.

questions.explanation: True. The model has no way to choose the subject of the query. A call with { userId: "u_5531" } fails validation because additionalProperties is false, and even a call that slipped past validation would not matter, because the handler ignores its arguments and reads ctx.userId, which the server takes from the authenticated session (u_2048). The common misconception is that a stricter description or system prompt ("only read the current user") gives the same protection: text asks the model to behave, while the tool design removes the possibility. The absolute wording is correct here because identity is decided entirely on the server.

False. Tool annotations describe a tool to the host; they are hints, and nothing in the protocol makes the server behave as the annotation claims. This handler inserts a row on every call, so the first call (which kept running on the server after the client timed out) and the retry most likely saved two plans. Idempotency has to be implemented by the server: an idempotency key that the host creates at confirmation time, stored with the first result and scoped to the session's user, so a repeat returns the same planId instead of inserting again. The common misconception is that a declared property is an enforced one; the spec says clients must not rely on annotations from untrusted servers for safety decisions.
